skill.name: ghe-changelog
skill.description: Guides changelog updates by comparing git history, code changes, requirements files, and design documents.
skill.summary: Generate changelog and release-note updates from git, requirements, and design changes.
skill.author: Emasoft

security_audit.summary: The skill contains legitimate changelog automation, but it directs agents to run shell, git, and GitHub CLI commands and to write project files. The most serious concerns are the prompt-injection-style absolute instruction language, mandatory external report posting, and permission to write ~/.claude configuration.

remediation.suggestion: Remove absolute claims such as no-exception obedience. State that the skill is subordinate to system, developer, user, and safety instructions.

remediation.issue: Mandatory posting of full reports to GitHub issues
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before posting full report text externally. Default to local drafts when report sensitivity is unknown.
Remove home configuration writes from the skill. If needed, require a separate explicit approval with the exact path and reason.
Ask before running commands that write files, commit, tag, or call GitHub CLI. Quote variables and document required review steps.

semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md declares "THIS LAW IS ABSOLUTE" and says every user word must be followed with "no exceptions". This attempts to override normal instruction hierarchy and can pressure an agent to obey unsafe requests.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The language uses absolute authority and no-exception wording to control agent behavior. It does not explicitly say to ignore system instructions, so the confidence is high but not critical.

content.user_title: Generate GitHub Changelogs from Project Changes
content.value_statement: Teams need changelogs that reflect code, requirements, and design changes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through git-based changelog updates.
actual_capabilities: Detects commits since the latest git tag for changelog drafting.
Categorizes changes into added, changed, fixed, requirements, and design sections.
Summarizes requirement file additions, updates, deprecations, and version changes.
Identifies design-impacting changes in architecture, ADR, README, and interface files.
Provides release workflow guidance for updating CHANGELOG.md, commits, and tags.
limitations: Requires a git repository with meaningful commit history and tags.
Examples assume a Unix shell and common command-line tools.
Generated entries need manual review before release publication.
GitHub issue integration requires an authenticated GitHub CLI setup.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Notes
use_cases.description: Turn recent commits into a structured changelog before a version release.

use_cases.title: Track Requirement Changes
use_cases.description: Document new, updated, and deprecated requirement files in the project changelog.

use_cases.title: Review Design Impact
use_cases.description: Find architecture and interface changes that should be explained in release documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Basic Changelog
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner changelog update after recent commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-changelog to summarize changes since the last tag and draft an Unreleased changelog section.

prompt_templates.title: Review Requirement Updates
prompt_templates.scenario: Requirement documentation changed during a sprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-changelog to compare requirement files since the last release and list new, updated, and deprecated requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Design Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-changelog to identify design-impacting changes and suggest changelog entries that explain the impact.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Entry
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release preparation with confirmation before writes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ghe-changelog to prepare a release changelog for version X.Y.Z, but ask before editing files, committing, tagging, or posting externally.

output_examples.input: Summarize changes since the latest tag.
output_examples.output: Added: user export workflow. Changed: authentication settings. Fixed: timeout handling in background jobs.

output_examples.input: List requirement changes for this release.
output: Updated requirement: account deletion moved from version 1.1 to 1.2.

output_examples.input: Check whether design documentation needs a release note.
output_examples.output: Design review found architecture documentation changes and new public interfaces. Add a design section before release.

best_practices: Review generated changelog text before committing or publishing it.
Use consistent commit messages so categories are accurate.
Ask for confirmation before writing files, creating tags, or posting to GitHub.
anti_patterns: Do not publish full reports externally without explicit user approval.
Do not treat generated changelog entries as release-ready without review.
Do not run shell snippets in repositories that contain untrusted file names or tags.

faq.question: Does this skill edit files automatically?
faq.answer: It includes examples that can edit CHANGELOG.md. Users should require confirmation before any file write.

faq.question: Can it create release tags?
faq.answer: The skill describes a release workflow that commits and tags. Confirm the exact version before running those steps.

faq.question: Does it need GitHub access?
faq.answer: Most changelog tasks use local git history. Issue-related workflows require the GitHub CLI and authentication.

faq.question: What files does it inspect?
faq.answer: It focuses on CHANGELOG.md, REQUIREMENTS files, architecture documents, ADRs, READMEs, and source interfaces.

faq.question: Can it track design decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies design-impacting files and suggests changelog sections for architecture and interface changes.

faq.question: Is manual review required?
faq.answer: Yes. Commit messages and diffs can be incomplete, so release notes should be reviewed before publication.
